reading: The heteronym resolves as a heteronym of the archive, placed in the Dodecad. Both works named are real: 14.CHAMBER.THOUSANDWORLDS (#14, creator 'Sen Kuro (Primary Operative)'; Zenodo creators Kuro, Sen and Sharks, Lee) with its Dagger Logic, and the Diversity Contraction boundary law. The second carries a split attribution. The archive registry seats #779 under Nobel Glas alone; the Zenodo metadata for the later versions in the family (Fear and Trembling; The Bead Count) lists four creators — Sharks, Fraction, Glas, Kuro — and the composition credits the work to Kuro. It follows the platform's creator line and keeps the Zenodo records as live sources, although the archive's Zenodo account was severed.
analysis: At the severed platform the heteronym still holds, with the archive named and the Dodecad as its frame, while the orthonym drops out. What the surface cannot see is the attribution difference between the archive's registry and the platform's metadata; it takes the platform's multi-creator line and narrows it to the queried name. 'Prominent avant-garde author' is the layer's own descriptor and appears in no card.
